text:
alex: CI regression flagged on long-context FP8 run — single-host end-to-end latency up ~2x for the 8k token workload. TTFT and tail look worse after the kernel selector change yesterday.

jordan: which change? the kernel routing PR?

alex: yeah PR #4128 — it introduced a per-layer kernel switch that tries to pick int8/4bit for smaller layers and fp8 for attention. appears fine on short ctx, but for 8k we see a lot of stalls during the early prefill window.

sam: can you paste the profiler flame or perf counters?

alex: pasted below (trimmed). notice repeated memcpy + kernel-swap around layer 10-14 during prefill: 
```
prefill: layer 1-9: fp8-kernel (shared)
layer 10: switch -> int8-opt (cache miss) 
memcpy 3.2ms 
queue sync 2.8ms 
layer 11: switch -> fp8-kernel 
memcpy 3.1ms 
...
end prefill TTFT: 190ms (baseline 85ms)
TPS: 90/s (baseline 120/s)
```

maria: that memcpy+sync pattern smells like kernel binary swap causing device-side stalling. maybe the selector is loading kernels lazily on first use and blocking the stream.

nate: also saw KV cache churn on the same runs — when the selector switches kernel layout it changes kv tile packing, which invalidates some cached prefixes and forces re-serialize. Could be double penalty: kernel load + kv re-materialize.

jordan: good call. can we repro with --no-kernel-lazy-load?

alex: repro with `--kernel-preload=all` reduces TTFT back to ~95ms but TPS still 102/s (still a small gap). so kernel load was big part but not all.

sam: paste svmem and GPU timeline for the run with preload enabled? curious if PCIe copies still happen.

alex: snippet: 
```
with preload: memcpy spikes drop, but there are repeated small memset/copy at decode boundaries ~0.6ms each.
KV ops: eviction spike at token 2048 and 4096 (LRU bump), re-encode cost ~1.9ms each.
```

maria: eviction at 2048/4096 suggests our KV block size isn't aligned with the quantized tile size. if fp8 packs differently we might be miscalculating offsets and causing extra copies when we rebase the cache.

nate: workaround: increase kv_block_bytes to align with quantized_row_bytes (set to 256 -> 320). temporary patch reduces re-encode cost but increases memory footprint ~6%.

jordan: ok tradeoff matrix: TTFT vs TPS vs memory. We should quantify regression: 
- baseline (float16 kernels): TTFT 85ms, TPS 120/s, mem 12GB
- post-selector (lazy): TTFT 190ms, TPS 90/s, mem 11.2GB
- post-selector (preload+kv-align): TTFT 98ms, TPS 112/s, mem 12.7GB

sam: that looks promising. another angle: batching heuristics. our microbatch scheduler folds a bunch of short requests into prefill windows — with kernel swaps we get stragglers and the scheduler lengthens TTFT to accommodate regulation. Maybe fallback: if estimated longctx > 4k, force unified-kernel mode for prefill and only switch to mixed post-prefill.

alex: interesting: force-unified reduced complexity: TTFT 105ms, TPS 115/s, no KV churn. Implementation is simple: add a ctx-size heuristic in router.

maria: but careful - unified mode loses per-layer quant gains for throughput. need to gate by customer tier. for heavy batch workloads might cost more.

nate: action items:
- (alex) open quick revert of lazy kernel load for canary cluster and enable kernel-preload on perf job (P0)
- (sam) prototype router heuristic: if requested_ctx_tokens >= 4096 -> unified-prefill-mode (P1)
- (jordan) add kv_block alignment test to quant CI matrix (P1)
- (maria) run cost simulation for memory bump vs TPS gain (P2)

ci-bot: perf-check: canary cluster with kernel-preload shows 1.15x lower 95p latency for 8k workload; alert cleared for now but leaving flag off prod until formal rollout.

alex: thanks — I'll send a short doc summarizing findings and include the profiling snippets + config diff. we should also update the kernel selector to avoid loading binaries on-the-fly (lazy->async-preload) and add telemetry for kernel-load time.

maria: +1. also add a golden test that runs 8k longctx FP8 path in CI to catch this next time.

jordan: reassigning PR #4128 to eng-runtime for follow-up.

sam: happy to help with the microbench harness if you want isolation tests for TTFT vs TPS.

alex: will loop you in. :thumbsup:
